claims.text: In high-temperature sliding of FeNiCrCoCu coatings, wear resistance and microscopic deformation are primarily governed by formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline, partially amorphous tribolayer exhibiting inverse Hall–Petch behavior.
The refined tribolayer accommodates shear through multiple deformation pathways.
Formation of the refined tribolayer reduces wear and stabilizes microscopic deformation.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse microstructure.
A pre-sliding thermal or processing treatment can promote near-surface grain refinement in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Pre-sliding near-surface refinement favors rapid dynamic amorphization during subsequent sliding.
Elevated temperature increases diffusion and dislocation mobility during sliding.
Friction-induced heat and stress enhance tribolayer formation.
The ultra-nanocrystalline, partially amorphous near-surface layer alters grain-boundary structure and dislocation pathways.
Under high-temperature sliding, thermal activation and mechanical stress dynamically refine coarse FeNiCrCoCu grains into a nanocrystalline tribolayer.
The refined tribolayer reduces local shear strength through inverse Hall–Petch behavior.
The refined layer redistributes deformation by activating multiple slip systems.
The pre-treated coating will form a more pronounced ultra-nanocrystalline tribolayer than the untreated baseline during sliding.
The pre-treated coating will have a lower wear rate than the untreated baseline.
The pre-treated coating will exhibit less micro-cracking and cavitation than the untreated baseline.
The untreated baseline forms an adaptive tribolayer less efficiently than the pre-treated coating.
The proposed mechanism should dominate at high operating temperatures but may not dominate at lower temperatures or under static conditions.
Inverse Hall–Petch behavior, dynamic amorphization, and ultra-nanocrystalline tribolayer formation have been observed in CoCrFeMnNi.
